gInvariants.text: Ledger balance: Σ finalized sale totals − Σ refunds = Σ net tender movements (per tender type).
Cash drawer: expected cash = opening float + cash sales − cash refunds − payouts (incl. trade-in payouts, supplier cash) ± drops/pickups.
Totals: per document Σ line totals − discounts = document total exactly; Σ document totals = report totals.
Stock: opening + purchases − sold + returned (restocked) ± adjustments = on-hand, per product and per serial/IMEI; no negative stock unless oversell is allowed by rule.
Serial uniqueness: each IMEI/serial exists in exactly one place/state (in stock, sold, in repair, with customer, returned to supplier).
Numbering: receipt/invoice/ticket numbers unique; sequence per rule (gapless or gaps logged).
Loyalty: balance = Σ earned − Σ redeemed − Σ reversed − Σ expired (≥ 0 unless the owner allows negative); no points from voided/refunded sales survive.
Audit: every money/stock/loyalty/role mutation has an audit entry; hash chain verifies; entries immutable.
Idempotency: replaying any request with the same idempotency key creates no second effect.
Atomicity: after crash/kill at any point, each business transaction is fully present or fully absent (sale+lines+payments+stock+loyalty+audit together).
Three-way equality: UI value = stored value = printed/exported value = oracle value (integer minor units).
Sync convergence: after all devices sync and settle, every device has identical ledger totals and identical row sets for money tables.
Referential integrity: `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` empty; `PRAGMA integrity_check` = ok.
No float money: no non-integer value ever stored or computed for money/qty-in-milli.
Permissions: no action succeeds for a role that must not have it (checked via attempted-forbidden actions in the random walk).
Resource budget: memory/handle/DB-size growth stays within budget; p95 latency not degrading > 2× from baseline.

One open drawer session per drawer: at most one `open` session per drawer id across all devices; every open/close carries a monotonic version; opened-by user, float and times are identical on every device once settled.

Cross-device freshness: drawer/shift/ticket status shown on any device equals the server state within the configured SLA while online; when it cannot be verified (offline or stale beyond a threshold) the UI says "unknown, last synced HH:MM" and blocks actions that need fresh state.

Attribution: every document (sale, refund, payout, trade-in, ticket, inspection, drawer event) stores `user_id` + display-name snapshot + device + drawer taken from the authenticated session, never from client-supplied fields; the name printed/exported equals the stored snapshot.

Session integrity: no mutation is accepted without a valid session; after logout, lock, user switch or disable, the next mutation is rejected or re-authenticated; an open cart never silently changes owner.

Warranty: each active warranty is bound to exactly one device (all IMEIs of a dual-SIM phone) and one source document; eligibility = f(stored dates, policy stored at sale time, current claim count); claims never exceed the policy.

Query-plan guard: every hot query (search, list page, lookup by IMEI/phone/ticket) uses an index (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` shows no `SCAN` of a big table) and its latency stays within tolerance across the 1 k / 100 k / 1 M fixtures.

Customer identity: the normalized phone is unique among active customers (or the duplicate is flagged); a merge leaves a `merged_into` redirect so late-arriving rows from other devices still land on the survivor.

Outbox: every locally created, unsynced record sits in a persisted outbox with an idempotency key; the count is visible to the user; nothing is discarded from a device (logout, update, uninstall prompt) until the backend acknowledges it.
Platform parity: the same inputs give identical money results, names and statuses on desktop and mobile builds (integer minor units).
Blob/reference integrity: every photo/scan reference resolves to a stored file or is explicitly "pending upload"; no orphan files or dangling references after settle.

Acknowledged = durable: any sale, refund, payout or drawer event the user was told succeeded (screen confirmation, printed slip, cash out, card approval) survives `kill -9` and power loss, or the owner-accepted durability policy states exactly what can be lost.

Recoverability: the newest backup restores into a DB that passes `integrity_check`, equals the source ledger totals at backup time and has a valid hash chain; backup age ≤ the owner's RPO; at least one copy is off the machine.

Refund conservation: for every sale line Σ refunded qty ≤ sold qty and Σ refunded amount ≤ net paid share; for every tender Σ refunds ≤ amount paid with it; enforced in the database layer, not only in the UI.

No destructive cascade: deleting or merging a customer/product/user/device never deletes or edits ledger rows (sales, lines, payments, refunds, stock moves, loyalty, audit); ledger rows are never rewritten or deleted except by the audited retention job.
Scale budget: hot-path latency, DB size, WAL size and backup/restore time stay within owner-agreed budgets at the projected 3-year volume (customers, sales, lines, products, IMEIs, audit rows).

Account balance: per customer (credit sales, instalments, deposits, store credit) balance = Σ sales − Σ payments − Σ credit notes − Σ write-offs; a negative balance exists only as an explicit credit; equals the ledger oracle.

Type discipline: money, quantity and counter columns hold integers; IMEI, phone, receipt/ticket numbers and ids hold TEXT; enforced by `STRICT` or `CHECK(typeof())`; a `typeof()` audit finds 0 violations after import, sync apply and migration.

Derived data is rebuildable: every derived table or column (counters, stock balances, summaries, FTS, normalized search columns, refunded counters) can be rebuilt from ledger rows and equals the stored value.

Destructive-change guard: an operation that deletes or overwrites more than N rows, or touches a ledger table, passes the guard (preview, restore point, step-up, audit) or fails; the same guard applies to sync-applied changes.
Unique device identity: each live `device_id` appears once; ID and document-number ranges of different devices never overlap; a clone or restored image is detected and re-registered.
